about: A rearranged version of Zork I. You collect treasures, carry them to the trophy case in the white house, and score points. The map is different in places. The studio chimney gives a way back up, the Round Room is a hub, and the coal mine is a trap.

done.why: I was stuck in the coal mine. A vampire bat carried me back into the mine maze every time I entered its room, and that room was the only way out. I had left the pepper-smelling sack in the studio, so I could not get past the bat and gave up there.

moments.note: Taking the painting scored 39 points right away, much more than the classic game gives.
The chimney carries only the lantern and one other item, so I had to drop things and make several trips.
Pressing the yellow button, turning the bolt with the wrench, and waiting drained the reservoir. That exposed the trunk of jewels.
The egg was in the nest up the tree and went into the trophy case for points.
The bat carried me off every time I entered its room, and I could not get past it.
Every coal mine room is named 'Coal Mine', so the maze gave me no way to tell rooms apart.
The Timber Room slot refused even the lantern, so the machine room was out of reach.

wished: Garlic or some other way past the bat.
A clearer sign of which Coal Mine room I was in.
A way back up from the mine other than the bat room.

lines.line: With great effort, you open the window far enough to allow entry.
lines.why: I recognised this as the start of the classic route in.

lines.line: You can't get up there with what you're carrying... The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It told me the exact carry limit and why I could not climb.

fun.why: Collecting treasures and draining the reservoir were satisfying. The bat and the mine maze left me stuck.

engagement.why: I always had a clear goal of finding the next treasure and getting it to the trophy case.

difficulty.why: The mine maze with identical room names and the bat gate were hard to get through.

interestingness.why: The altered map and scoring were interesting, but I could not see most of the changes.

prose.why: Classic Zork prose that is clear and functional, with a few good touches.
